source_text: Opponents of routine male circumcision contend that it constitutes an elective procedure lacking sufficient medical necessity for healthy newborns, as the conditions it aims to prevent—such as urinary tract infections (UTIs), penile cancer, and certain sexually transmitted infections (STIs)—occur infrequently enough in uncircumcised populations to render the intervention non-essential. [6] [124]
